comparator.name: Communicatiewetenschap
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current study-programme page publishes a complete 180-EC curriculum: 60 EC in each year. Years 1 and 2 comprise communication domains, statistics and research methods, an internship and communication advice. Year 3 comprises 30 EC of elective space, an 18-EC graduation project and 12 EC of communication-science topics. The graduation project requires one of four directions; Corporate Communicatie is selected by the neutral first-listed rule.
components: Genuine elective space; no specific minor or courses are invented.
Corporate Communicatie is selected by the neutral first-listed route rule.
Two communication-science topics chosen from the published bound-choice space.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the Dutch Communication Science programme and does not privilege one graduation-project direction. Corporate Communicatie is the first option listed on the official programme page, so it is selected before comparison with UCR.

core: Communication theory, media, persuasion and effects on people and society
Quantitative, qualitative and experimental communication research
Corporate, entertainment, persuasive and political communication domains
adjacent: Corporate, persuasive, marketing and health communication
questions: How do media and communication affect people, behaviour and society?
How can messages and communication strategies achieve organisational, health or social goals?
How do journalism, political communication and media trust shape democracy?

alternatives.label: Communication, Media & Society
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible communication-science pathway combining rhetoric, persuasion, media analysis, organisational and political communication, social psychology and quantitative and qualitative research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum visibly combines communication, media, society, persuasion and empirical research without implying a dedicated professional Communication Science degree.
progression: Communication and media foundations precede advanced persuasion, documentary, organisational and applied communication; social-science, psychology and data courses provide a coherent empirical progression. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with six 300-level courses.

alternatives.label: Persuasion, Marketing & Health Communication
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines health and behavioural evidence with persuasion, organisational communication, media and empirical methods; the label states those visible strands directly.
alternatives.concept: Builds the evidenced persuasive, marketing and health-communication direction around rhetoric, behavioural science, public health, disease, ethics, quantitative and qualitative research and applied communication design.
progression: Life-science, public-health, psychology, communication, data and research foundations precede health psychology, disease study, persuasion and applied communication. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with seven 300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes behaviour, health and marketing the application domains for persuasion and communication; it differs from the broad closest match by more than four courses and 30 EC.

alternatives.label: Political Communication, Journalism & Public Trust
alternatives.concept: Builds the evidenced political-communication and journalism direction around media, rhetoric, democratic institutions, sociology, public trust, qualitative and quantitative methods.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines politics, media, persuasion, sociology and public-trust analysis with empirical research methods.
alternatives.distinctness: This route centres democratic politics, journalism and public trust; it differs from both the broad communication pathway and the health-focused pathway by more than four courses and 30 EC.
progression: Political, media, communication, sociology, psychology and data foundations precede advanced political communication, media analysis and public-trust study. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with seven 300-level courses.

blocks: Both introduce theoretically informed analysis of communication and rhetoric.
Both provide a foundation for analysing media forms and institutions.
Both support systematic analysis of audiovisual and media content.
Both examine persuasion, message effects and audience response.
Both analyse public rhetoric and communication in relation to power and politics.
Both move from communication analysis toward applied communication design and advice.
Both develop qualitative research design and analysis.
Both examine communication, leadership and relationships in organisational settings.
Both use empirical behavioural research to study effects on people.
Both develop statistical and experimental methods for human-behaviour research.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme-defining communication-science, media-effects and empirical-research interests. Persuasion/marketing/health and political communication/journalism are the two strongest coherent remaining directions and yield feasible, substantively distinct programmes. Entertainment and global/intercultural communication remain coherent candidates but cannot be added after the three-alternative maximum is reached.

notes.text: UvA provides a dedicated Communication Science curriculum with a sequenced methods spine, internship, advice course and 18-EC graduation project. UCR can combine rhetoric, media, politics, behavioural science and empirical methods, but does not reproduce that professional and disciplinary structure.

The selected UvA target is the Dutch-taught Communicatiewetenschap track; UCR is English-taught. Global Communication Science is a distinct English track and is not substituted for the normalized target.
